# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).
- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.
- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `<Box sx={{ flex: 1 }} />` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.
- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.

---

## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions

- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).
- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.
- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.
- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.
- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.

---

## 5. Borders & elevation

- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).
- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.
- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.
- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.
- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.

---

## 6. Typography usage

Drive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.

- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.
- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).
- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant="overline"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).
- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.
- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.

---

## 7. Interaction states

Consistent across all components; all colors from the theme:

- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.
- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.
- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.
- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.
- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.
- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).
- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.
- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.

---

## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)

- **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).
- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.
- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.
- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.
- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.
- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.
- **Select:** `size="small"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.
- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.
- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). ```text
DataService
â”œâ”€ ProjectState              project, files and parsed card snapshot
â”œâ”€ CardOperations           card/file mutations
â”œâ”€ ProjectLoading           loading, watching and refresh
â”œâ”€ AgentIntegration         conversations attached to cards

â””â”€ SaveStateService         pending-save state

Separate application services
â”œâ”€ OpenFilesService         open paths and active path
â”œâ”€ WorkspaceViewService     selected path and view mode
â”œâ”€ ActionService            definitions and drafts by source path
â”œâ”€ ActionExecutionService   live executions and path-based contexts
â”œâ”€ WorktreeService          worktree records
â””â”€ ConfigService            resolved application/project configuration
```

The resulting identity inconsistency is:

```text
Persisted card relationships â†’ internalId
UI and editing state          â†’ path
Agent/card association        â†’ path
Action execution              â†’ actionId + path-based context
Storage operations            â†’ path
```

So React already has a stable internal card identity available, but much of its runtime model still treats the mutable filepath as the card/file identity.

    ActionRunnerService ..> ActionExecutionService : execution events via bridge
    LocalGitStorageService --> ElectronPreloadBridge : local data bridge
    RemoteControlStorageService --> RemoteControlService : WebSocket bridge
```

`main.js` composes the desktop service graph. `ActionRunnerService` owns per-run `ActionExecution` instances; `ActionSchedulerService` starts those same executions for timers. `AgentRunnerService` owns child processes and creates a protocol parser for each provider stream. `LocalBridgeDispatch` exposes the graph both to the Electron preload IPC bridge and to `RemoteControlService`, which is how the app-side classes in the first diagram reach the same desktop services.

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required so long content ellipsizes instead of blowing out the row).
- **Panels (sidebar, editor card, dialogs):** column flex with stacked bands (header / [toolbar] / body / footer). The **body scrolls** (`overflow-y: auto; minHeight: 0`); header and footer are `flexShrink: 0` and never scroll away.
- **Spacer pattern:** push trailing items with `<Box sx={{ flex: 1 }} />` rather than `margin-left: auto` sprinkled around, so rows stay predictable.
- Use flex `gap` for spacing between siblings â€” don't hand-space with per-child margins.

---

## 4. Spacing, margin & size conventions

- **4/8px grid, via `theme.spacing`.** page padding `2.5`; between columns `2`; inside columns / between related controls `1`; dialog body gap `2â€“2.25`; field labelâ†’control gap `~0.9` (7px).
- **Margins:** prefer padding on containers + flex `gap` over element margins. Where a floating panel needs breathing room (e.g. editor card, toolbar inside a panel), use container padding (`p: 2 / 2.5`), not margins on the children.
- **Fixed heights (px):** menu row 44, ribbon 52, status bar 32, section header 40, tab row 40, standard button / control 34, dense icon button 26â€“28, input 42.
- **Fixed widths (px):** column 296, sidebar 280, search 260, standard dialog 480, wide/editor dialog 760.
- **Radius family (px):** buttons/icon-buttons 8 (small 6â€“7), inputs 9, cards 10, columns/panels 12, dialogs/popups 14, chips/pills 99, color swatches 3. `borderRadius: 1` covers the 8 case; use explicit `'9px'` etc. for the others.

---

## 5. Borders & elevation

- **Rest = border, not shadow.** Resting surfaces: `border: '1px solid'`, `borderColor: 'divider'`. Inputs use `custom.borderStrong`. **Shadow only when floating or lifted** (hover, drag, dialogs/popovers).
- **Separation between bands:** a single 1px `divider` hairline. Don't stack a heavy rule *and* an outline â€” one line, let background contrast do the rest. Vertical separators inside toolbars: a 20px-tall `custom.borderStrong` rule.
- **Elevation ladder (only where floating):** card hover `0 4px 12px rgba(16,24,40,0.12)`; dragging MUI `elevation 8` + `rotate(2deg)`; contained button `0 1px 2px rgba(16,24,40,0.15)`; dialog/popup `0 24px 60px rgba(16,24,40,0.28)`; scrim `rgba(16,24,40,0.45)` + `backdropFilter: blur(2px)`.
- Set `MuiPaper.elevation: 0` and `MuiButton.disableElevation` globally in the theme; add the shadows above explicitly where the ladder calls for it.
- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** â€” the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.

---

## 6. Typography usage

Drive everything from theme variants / `theme.typography`; avoid ad-hoc `fontSize`.

- Titles/values/headings â†’ `text.primary`; body & labels â†’ `text.secondary`; meta â†’ `custom.text3`.
- **Field labels:** a plain `Typography` (12px/600, `text.secondary`) placed **above** the control â€” **never** MUI floating/outlined `TextField` labels (they clash with the app's flat-label style).
- **Section/column headers:** `Typography variant="overline"` (uppercase, `letterSpacing ~0.7px`, `fontWeight 700`, `custom.colHead`).
- **ID chips only** use monospace; everything else is the theme's default family.
- `button.textTransform: 'none'` and `button.fontWeight: 600` are set in the theme â€” don't re-uppercase buttons.

---

## 7. Interaction states

Consistent across all components; all colors from the theme:

- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent â†’ hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.
- **Outlined button:** `divider` border, `text.secondary` â†’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.
- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.
- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.
- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.
- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).
- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.
- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.

---

## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)

- **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).
- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.
- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.
- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.
- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.
- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.
- **Select:** `size="small"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.
- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.
- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop.
- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No "click to add" placeholder blocks.

---

## 9. Definition of done for a new component

1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.
2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.
3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.
4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.
5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.
6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).

Component-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.

`DataService` is the main renderer domain aggregate: it owns the project state and workflow classes, while global singleton services communicate through direct imports or `EventTarget`. Persistence is selected per project through `StorageService`. Local Electron, remote-control, and GitHub implementations therefore feed the same app-side workflows. Component arrows show direct rendering, component-as-prop usage, portal/plugin composition, and the principal service dependencies; components without project-defined children remain as leaf nodes.

`main.js` composes the desktop service graph. `ActionRunnerService` owns per-run `ActionExecution` instances; `ActionSchedulerService` starts those same executions for timers. `AgentRunnerService` owns child processes and creates a protocol parser for each provider stream. `LocalBridgeDispatch` exposes the graph both to the Electron preload IPC bridge and to `RemoteControlService`, which is how the app-side classes in the first diagram reach the same desktop services.

command is run on a card that is assigned to a worktree, the worktree selector icon is not updated and the wrong state is shown on the card. if the user clicks again on the icon and runs the 'integrate into project' again, the app gives an error to say nothing left to integrate. then the icon gets updated correctly\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` derives its arrows and enabled actions from records published by `WorktreeService`. Integration creates a squash commit on the project branch, but leaves the linked branch on its original commits. Git therefore still reports the worktree as ahead and behind. Keep its assignment and branch; do not park or unassign it.\\r\\n- After card activity persistence completes, synchronize the linked branch to the new project head and publish worktree state again.\\r\\n- Keep project-level integration on the shared synchronization path; it needs no activity refresh.\\r\\n- Preserve existing integration and activity-persistence errors. Existing renderer subscription should update without component-local state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Successful integration immediately removes the outgoing indicator and disables `Integrate into project`.\\r\\n- Card integration finishes with no outgoing or incoming indicator and disables both integration and update actions.\\r\\n- Reopening the selector or waiting for polling is unnecessary.\\r\\n- A second integration is not required to correct the icon and is unavailable when no outgoing changes remain.\\r\\n- Card and project integrations publish correct final worktree status; failure behavior remains unchanged.\\r\\n\\n===== B_81_new_card_markdown_typing_lag.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: B_81\\r\\ninternalId: 8e4a295a-8788-4232-8be7-c97f5a1cf5c8\\r\\ntitle: new card Markdown typing lag\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Problem\\r\\n\\r\\nTyping in the **New card** description editor has noticeable input lag.\\r\\n\\r\\nPerformance trace `Trace-20260731T140458.json` records five input events that each block the renderer main thread for 52-64 ms. Layout and paint are small; synchronous React work consumes most of the time.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Cause\\r\\n\\r\\n`NewCardDialog` passes `handleBodyChange` to `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange`. Every editor change calls `setBody`, rerendering the complete dialog and the MDXEditor subtree. This also recreates the Markdown editor plugin array and many MUI elements and style objects. Development-mode React work and garbage collection amplify the cost.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis bypasses the lifetime-stable editor approach already used by `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`. `MarkdownEditor` already buffers local edits and exposes `getMarkdown`, `setMarkdown`, and `flush`; normal typing does not need to propagate the full body into parent React state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep the new-card Markdown editor lifetime-stable while typing, following `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`.\\r\\n- Do not store the full Markdown body in `NewCardDialog` state on every keystroke.\\r\\n- Read the current body from the editor when submitting, checking whether the draft is dirty, and inserting or clearing the template.\\r\\n- Preserve existing template behavior: untouched template can be cleared; editing it changes the action back to `Template`; inserting then appends without discarding text.\\r\\n- Keep reset, cancel confirmation, `Ctrl+Enter`, and target-column behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Do not change shared `MarkdownEditor` buffering semantics solely for this dialog.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Typing in the new-card description does not rerender `NewCardDialog` or remount/rerender the Markdown editor for every keystroke.\\r\\n- [ ] Submitted card body exactly matches current editor content.\\r\\n- [ ] Cancel confirmation detects description-only edits.\\r\\n- [ ] Template insert, clear, edit, and append behavior remains unchanged.\\r\\n- [ ] Opening, closing, successful creation, and project changes reset the draft correctly.\\r\\n- [ ] A regression test verifies repeated description edits do not repeatedly render the editor boundary.\\r\\n- [ ] Existing new-card dialog and Markdown editor tests pass.\\r\\n\\n===== B_82_orphaned_git_for_windows_processes.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: B_82\\r\\ninternalId: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\\r\\ntitle: agent runs leave orphaned Git for Windows processes\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Problem\\r\\n\\r\\nAgent runs launched through MDÂ² can leave multiple `git.exe` processes running indefinitely. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\\r\\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\\r\\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\\r\\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\\r\\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\\r\\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\\r\\n\\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_115\\r\\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\ntitle: add support for request approval\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\n---\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. form and the same state:\\r\\n\\r\\n* **Desktop** â€” centered modal dialog over a scrim.\\r\\n* **Mobile** â€” full-height sheet.\\r\\n\\r\\nSame fields, same validation, same submit behavior. Never hard-code hex values per type; if a type has no color, fall back to a neutral token (`--text-4`).\\r\\n* Selected state: tinted background + border in the app's primary token, primary text color. Unselected: subtle track background, secondary text, transparent border; hover raises contrast.\\r\\n* Default selection: the app's existing default type (first in the list if there is no configured default).\\r\\n* Overflow: desktop wraps to multiple lines; mobile scrolls horizontally in one row (no wrap, no visible scrollbar chrome).\\r\\n* Keyboard: arrow keys move between pills, Space/Enter selects; the row is a single tab stop (radiogroup semantics â€” `role=\\\"radiogroup\\\"` with `role=\\\"radio\\\"` + `aria-checked` children).\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== F_91_remove_finished_reasoning_blocks.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_91\\r\\ninternalId: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\ntitle: remove finished reasoning blocks\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen a reasoning output of an agent finishes, we should remove the block\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\nCodex reasoning is stored as an `AgentConversationEvent`. Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\\r\\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\\r\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `<projectFolder>/<releasesFolder>`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n  - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Keep the existing terminal linking and loading test.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- A card-scoped `agentStarted` update adds the conversation reference to the card immediately, without waiting for completion.\\r\\n- If the app closes during the conversation after that card save is persisted, reopening the project still shows the reference in the card header.\\r\\n- A continuation or terminal event does not add the same reference twice.\\r\\n- Existing activity-file persistence behavior is unchanged.\\r\\n\\n===== F_102_select_empty_conversation.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_102\\r\\ninternalId: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\ntitle: select empty conversation\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 8e4a295a-8788-4232-8be7-c97f5a1cf5c8\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an action has historical logs and the user selects one, he is no longer able to select an empty 'conversation'\\r\\n\\r\\nThe first item in the context menu is disabled. This is wrong, the user should be able to select it so that he can go back to an empty conversation (the 'now' conversation)\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionConversationPicker` displays `Conversations` as its empty item but disables it. After history is selected, `handleConversationChange` only loads persisted paths, so popup cannot return to empty conversation state.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep empty `Conversations` item selectable while picker is enabled.\\r\\n- Treat empty value as reset: clear selected conversation and displayed chat without calling conversation loader.\\r\\n- Next run omits `continueFrom` and starts new conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- User can select `Conversations` after selecting historical conversation.\\r\\n- Popup returns to empty conversation without error or empty-path load.\\r\\n- Next run starts new conversation; selecting history still continues selected conversation.\\r\\n- Picker and controller tests cover reset and continuation behavior.\\r\\n\\n===== F_115_add_support_for_request_approval.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_115\\r\\ninternalId: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\r\\ntitle: add support for request approval\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\n---\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`CodexStreamingAdapter` handles structured questions, but not Codex app-server approval requests. `item/fileChange/requestApproval` and `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` fall through as protocol diagnostics, for example `item/fileChange/requestApproval: unknown (...)`. No approval UI or JSON-RPC response exists, so the turn remains blocked.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Handle both approval methods as server-initiated JSON-RPC requests before notification handling. Validate request, item, thread, and turn ids; track pending requests by request id; clear them on `serverRequest/resolved`.\\r\\n- Add a dedicated approval contract through `AgentRunnerService`, action execution events, Electron preload/local bridge, and remote control. Respond with `{ decision }`; for command requests, honor `availableDecisions` when supplied. Keep approvals separate from structured questions and conversation messages.\\r\\n- Store pending approvals in `ActionExecutionService`. Keep execution `waitingForInput` while any question or approval remains. Replay must restore unresolved approvals and discard resolved ones after renderer reload.\\r\\n- Add a separate popup approval component. Show reason plus command, working directory, parsed actions, network host/protocol, requested permissions, or affected file paths when available. Actions sit bottom-right: allow once, allow for session, decline, and stop turn. Show policy-amendment choices only when Codex supplies them.\\r\\n- Support multiple pending approvals without overwriting one another. Disable a submitted request until response or resolution; reject duplicate, stale, mismatched, or unsupported decisions clearly.\\r\\n- Do not persist approval requests or decisions in conversation/activity files or agent handoff context. Existing completed command/file activity remains authoritative.\\r\\n- Add adapter, runner, execution-contract, bridge, remote-control, service, popup, reload, and regression tests. Run lint and tests in `desktop/` and `app/`.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- File-change and command-execution approval requests show actionable prompts instead of protocol diagnostics.\\r\\n- Allow once/session, decline, stop-turn, and offered policy-amendment choices send the exact matching JSON-RPC decision and unblock Codex.\\r\\n- Approval UI shows available security context before user decides, including network-specific context when present.\\r\\n- Concurrent requests remain isolated; `serverRequest/resolved`, turn completion, or cancellation removes only matching pending requests.\\r\\n- Renderer reload and remote-control clients retain correct pending approval state.\\r\\n- Structured questions, activity ordering, changed-path tracking, and conversation persistence keep existing behavior; approval data is not persisted.\\r\\n\\n===== F_89_add_support_for_clicking_on_links_in_chatlogs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_89\\r\\ninternalId: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\ntitle: add support for clicking on links in chatlogs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: e69b9faf-30dd-4ad6-9d99-7e6af4d18c76\\r\\n---\\r\\nSometimes the agent produces a link to a local project file. Otherwise, open it with vscode (externally)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionConversationChat` renders messages with `ReactMarkdown` without a custom link handler. Normalize separators and convert paths inside the active repository to repository-relative paths.\\r\\n- When the target is inside configured `projectFolder` and is either a Markdown file or a loaded action-definition JSON file, switch to list view and open its existing Markdown or action editor.\\r\\n- Open every other local project file in VS Code through the Electron bridge. Keep normal web-link behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Reject paths outside the active repository and missing targets without crashing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Clicking relative or absolute Windows links to Markdown files under configured `projectFolder` opens them in list view with the Markdown editor.\\r\\n- Clicking relative or absolute Windows links to action-definition JSON
